floor_history.headline: Recon: stale 119 migration pin killed — honest floor is 57/173 (insn-count already exact); residual is one OR-association copy + the count-1 comparand carrier, both pass-attributed from the .loop dump

Floor 57 -> 52 in pure ordinary C: declaring `complement` inside the inner loop spends loop.c's first move (threshold -= 3) so the `count - 1` comparand stays inline, which retires s1's variable-reuse

Floor 52 -> 31 in ordinary C: fold-const's associate: block aims the OR-chain constant (write it next to the OTHER term), a late `i = 0;` fixes the $s1/$s2 pair, and one arm-local `*dst++` swaps the s

Found the missing 173rd instruction: the target inlines dst++ on the COLOUR arm, not the zero-pixel arm — form f1 is 43/173 with a structurally exact inner loop, and its whole residual is a one-atom s

Enumerate modality: 4,488 spellings swept across four regions on three chassis, ZERO hit — the blend block's naming/order/operand space and the outer declaration block's ordering space are both exhaus

frontier.hypothesis: The src/dst seat is bought by declaration SCOPE or BLOCK STRUCTURE above the blend block, not by any spelling inside it — e.g. declaring src and dst outside the outer do-loop (assigned rather than initialised each iteration), or splitting/merging the two arms' enclosing braces so dst's references land in different basic blocks.
frontier.mechanism: s5 exhausted naming, declaration order and operand order inside the two blocks where the arithmetic lives, and s4 exhausted the reference-count spellings that the tree folds away. What was never varied is where src and dst are DECLARED relative to the outer do-loop and how the arm bodies are bracketed — both change the basic-block partition flow.c walks when it accumulates REG_N_REFS, and reg_n_refs is loop-depth weighted, so moving one dst reference into a deeper block is worth several units on its own.
frontier.next_probe: On the h1 chassis (42 / 173), enumerate the DECLARATION-SCOPE axis rather than the spelling axis: (i) hoist 'u16 *src, *dst;' to function scope with 'src = src_buf; dst = dst_buf;' at the top of the outer do-body; (ii) the same but with only dst hoisted; (iii) wrap the two arms in a single shared brace and in two separate braces; (iv) move the 'advance_dst:' label's dst++ into each arm's own block. Measure each with sandbox --disable all AND re-run tools/ra_solver/extract.py + simulate.py, checking build_insns stays 173 and whether 108 -> $a3 / 109 -> $a2. Do NOT re-probe blend-arm spellings — enum1/enum3/enum4 covered them.

frontier.hypothesis: The object model for 'rect' is wrong: it is currently a bare 's16 *' read through three different casts (s16*, u16*, s32*), and a struct-typed rect changes the addressing and the pressure at the LoadImage/StoreImage calls enough to move the src/dst seat.
frontier.mechanism: The target's 0x214-0x234 block has never been checked against a struct-typed rect. A struct member read is one base register plus a constant offset, where the current casts force a fresh cast-and-index expression each time; that changes both the number of RTL references attributed to the pointer pseudos and what the calls clobber across the loop. This is the one structural axis the ledger has never touched.
frontier.next_probe: Grep include/ for an existing PsyQ RECT declaration (x/y/w/h as s16) and for other BB2 callers that pass the same buffer to StoreImage/LoadImage; if a RECT type already exists in the TU, re-spell the parameter as 'RECT *rect' and measure on both the h1 and d4 chassis. Read tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/dumps/*.combine to confirm whether the cast chain survives to RTL before spending more than two measurements on it.

frontier.hypothesis: The DrawSync prototype width lead from s4 is real: the TU that compiled func_8003DE14 saw a wider return type for DrawSync than void/int, which widens the live set across the three DrawSync calls and moves the src/dst seat.
frontier.mechanism: The f1-chassis permuter's only sub-base find (290 vs 300) was widening 'extern void DrawSync(s32);' to 'extern long long DrawSync(s32);'. A DImode return makes the call clobber a register pair. The prototype-contradiction norm (memory reference sotn-prototype-struct-precedent-2026-08-10) says the bytes decide the declaration — but a permuter score delta alone is not evidence.
frontier.next_probe: Still OUT OF SCOPE for a func_8003DE14-only session, and it stays that way until the census is positive: grep the other DrawSync callers in src/code6cac_c2.c and check whether ANY of them shows a v0/v1 pair clobber that the current 'void' declaration does not predict. Only a positive census justifies a measurement; the declaration lives in the shared includes and would perturb every caller in the TU.
